title: Purchasing Assistant
description:
Purchasing Assistant - Poole - Up to £30,000

With real scope to build your procurement expertise, you'll be trusted with the accuracy that keeps supply moving, from purchase order to delivery.
Every order, every supplier relationship, every record: it all runs through you.

As a Purchasing Assistant, you will benefit from:
- Structured onboarding and ongoing training in procurement systems and processes
- Support to work towards a recognised procurement qualification such as CIPS
- A stable, well-organised working environment with clear processes to follow
- Exposure to a broad commodity area, building genuine specialist knowledge over time

As a Purchasing Assistant, your responsibilities will include:
- Schedule incoming materials against forecast demand to maintain continuity of supply
- Generate and issue purchase orders to nominated suppliers within your commodity area
- Manage supplier non-conformances alongside Quality and Technical teams, negotiating costs where required
- Expedite outstanding orders and flag supplier delays that could affect production
- Maintain accurate procurement and supply records within the ERP/MRP system
- Investigate supplier price discrepancies and obtain credit notes where necessary

As a Purchasing Assistant, your experience will include:
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel, including formula creation and checking
- Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems, ideally including Oracle
- Experience liaising with suppliers and building effective working relationships
- Strong office administration and organisational skills
- An interest in building a career in procurement within a manufacturing environment
- Willingness to work towards a qualification such as CIPS

If you're looking for a role where your accuracy and reliability are genuinely valued, this Purchasing Assistant position offers a clear path to build real procurement expertise. Apply today with an up-to-date CV or call Nina Cranidge at Rubicon for more information.

While Rubicon uses AI to help speed up processes across the business, every application is reviewed by a human to ensure the right decision is made.

title: Supply Chain Planner
description:
Supply Chain Planner

We are currently partnering with a fast-paced and growing organisation to recruit a Supply Chain planner. This role will take ownership of the end-to-end fulfilment process across a designated supplier category, ensuring supplier data is accurately maintained and operational processes run smoothly across internal systems.

Key Responsibilities
- Take full ownership of fulfilment activities for an assigned supplier category, ensuring accuracy and efficiency across all processes
- Provide key documentation and information to support inbound purchase orders, including:
- Import clearance coordination
- Management of manufacturing order tolerances
- Supporting supplier payments in line with agreed terms
- Plan, schedule and coordinate inbound container shipments with suppliers and 3 PL warehouse partners
- Forecast replenishment requirements for 3 PL locations based on historical demand trends and upcoming business activity
- Generate reporting and trend analysis to support inventory planning and operational decision-making
- Raise and manage purchase orders in line with departmental targets and system-driven requirements
- Ensure timely supplier acknowledgement of purchase orders, challenging discrepancies and escalating issues where required
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records across business systems, communicating any changes to relevant stakeholders
- Monitor purchase order progress and proactively expedite deliveries to maintain high service levels
- Manage supplier non-conformance reports (NCRs), ensuring issues are recorded, investigated and resolved promptly
- Track and report on supplier and product performance, including ensuring all applicable rebates are captured
- Prepare data, insights and reports to support supplier reviews and commercial negotiations
- Support wider team activities and undertake additional duties as required

Required Background & Experience
- Previous experience within supply chain, logistics or warehouse/distribution environments
- Experience working with multiple systems, ideally including warehouse management and ERP systems
- Strong background in data management, reporting and analysis
- Experience managing relationships with multiple suppliers and third-party logistics providers

Skills & Attributes
- Strong analytical capability, with experience in forecasting and data-driven decision making
- Advanced Excel skills, with the ability to manipulate and manage complex data sets
- Highly detail-oriented, with a focus on accuracy across supply chain processes
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively across suppliers and internal stakeholders
- Process-driven and disciplined approach to work
- Highly organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines
- Genuine interest in product, supplier performance and supply chain operations

For more information call the Southampton Branch or if you fit the above Apply Now.
